title: Spectral Analysis Chamber
description: A chemistry lab spectral analysis station where the AnisotropyBarnLamp serves as a tunable UV-Vis light source and the Corset acts as a molecular lattice model clamped in the analysis chamber. The user must calibrate the lamp wavelength, adjust beam intensity, position the lattice sample, and record absorption readings across multiple spectral bands to identify an unknown crystalline compound.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing a spectral analysis lab. Load AnisotropyBarnLamp.glb positioned at (-2, 1, 0) as the tunable light source and Corset.glb at (2, 0.5, 0) as the molecular lattice sample mounted on a rotating platform. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 3, 6) looking at origin with OrbitControls. Add ambient light (0.3 intensity) and a SpotLight parented to the lamp model that emits a visible colored beam (use a CylinderGeometry with transparent emissive material) directed at the Corset. Create an HTML overlay panel with these interactive steps: (1) Power toggle button that activates the lamp with a glow animation on the lamp mesh emissive property. (2) Wavelength slider (380-780nm) that changes the beam color and SpotLight color in real-time using wavelength-to-RGB conversion. (3) Intensity slider (0-100%) controlling SpotLight intensity and beam opacity. (4) Three rotation buttons (X/Y/Z) that rotate the Corset model by 45 degrees with smooth tweening to simulate sample orientation. (5) A 'Record Reading' button that captures current wavelength, intensity, and rotation state, storing up to 6 readings in a visible data table. (6) An 'Analyze' button enabled only after recording at least 4 readings across different wavelengths, which compares readings against a hidden reference dataset and displays a match percentage with compound identification result. Validate that readings span at least 3 distinct wavelength bands (UV/Visible/Near-IR). Add a subtle grid floor, dark lab background (0x1a1a2e), and post-processing bloom on the beam. Display step progress as 'Step X/6' in the corner. The Corset should cast shadows from the SpotLight onto a BackPlane behind it to visualize diffraction patterns.
